newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish minister says could strike again in Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Turkish minister says could strike again in Cyprus.

text.p: Defence Minister Turhan Tayan warned on Wednesday that Turkey would attack Cyprus if it needed to protect the Turkish Cypriot community in the north of the Mediterranean island.
"What was needed in 1974 and what did we do? We will do the same again. If needed, we will strike," Tayan told the state-run TRT television channel in an interview.

Turkey has accused the Cypriot government of trying to change the balance of forces on the island by a deal announced at the weekend to buy Russian anti-aircraft missiles that could neutralise Turkish air superiority.
Turkey invaded Cyprus in 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup attempt backed by the military then ruling Athens. Ankara keeps about 30,000 troops in north Cyprus.
Tayan said Turkey had no ambitions to grab land on Cyprus but would protect the Turkish Cypriot minority.
"It should be known that the Turkish republic feels a great sense of responsibility towards its Turkish kin in Cyprus," he said. "We will do what is necessary."
A Turkish Cypriot state set up in the north in 1983 is recognised only by Ankara. The internationally-recognised Cypriot government is run by Greek Cypriots.
"We are in favour of peace, harmony, equality and law in Cyprus. We are not aggressive and we are not after territory," Tayan said.
The United States is to send an envoy to the island at the weekend in hopes of reducing tensions between Greeks and Turks.

In an unusually strong statement, Washington on Monday deplored Cyprus' contract to buy the S-300 anti-aircraft missile system from Russia, saying it would introduce a destabilising new military element and complicate peace moves.
